Python.description: The easiest first language. Used in AI, automation, web and security scripting.

courses.title: CS50's Introduction to Programming with Python
courses.why: Short lectures, then real problem sets. Very beginner friendly.

courses.title: Python for Everybody
courses.why: Free book, videos and exercises from Dr. Chuck. Slow and clear.

courses.title: Scientific Computing with Python
courses.why: Write code in the browser. No setup needed.

courses.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
courses.why: Learn by building small useful scripts (files, web, Excel).

courses.title: CS50's Introduction to Artificial Intelligence with Python
courses.why: Next step after basics. Search, ML and neural networks with projects.

notes.title: Official Python Tutorial
notes.note: Accurate and free. Good to read next to any course.

notes.title: Automate the Boring Stuff (online book)
notes.note: Whole book is free to read online.

labs.title: Exercism - Python track
labs.note: Small exercises with free human-style feedback.

C++.description: Fast, powerful language for systems, games and competitive programming.

courses.title: Learn C++
courses.why: The most complete free C++ tutorial. Quizzes at the end of lessons.

courses.title: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.why: Teaches C first (memory and pointers). That makes C++ much easier later.

courses.title: Learn C++
courses.why: Type code in the browser. Some parts need a paid plan.

courses.title: CS106L: Standard C++ Programming
courses.why: Modern C++ (STL, templates, move semantics) with assignments.

notes.title: cppreference
notes.note: The standard reference. Search any function here.

notes.title: C++ Core Guidelines
notes.note: Best-practice rules by the language creators. Advanced reading.

labs.title: Exercism - C++ track
labs.note: Exercises that get harder step by step.

labs.title: Codeforces
labs.note: Contest problems. Good once you know the basics.

Cyber Security.description: Protecting systems and finding weaknesses legally. Learn by doing in safe labs.

courses.title: Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate
courses.why: Full beginner path (risk, Linux, SQL, SIEM). Certificate costs money, learning can be audited.

courses.title: TryHackMe Learning Paths
courses.why: Hands-on rooms in the browser. Many rooms are free, some need a subscription.

courses.title: Professor Messer - CompTIA Security+ videos
courses.why: Free full video course for the Security+ exam. Open the Security+ section.

courses.title: Web Security Academy
courses.why: Best free web-hacking course. Every topic has real labs.

notes.title: OWASP Top 10
notes.note: The 10 most common web security risks, explained.

notes.title: MITRE ATT&CK
notes.note: Reference of attacker techniques. Read, do not memorize.

labs.title: OverTheWire - Bandit
labs.note: Learn Linux commands by solving levels. Start here.

labs.title: PortSwigger Web Security Labs
labs.note: Free vulnerable apps to practice on.

labs.title: Hack The Box Academy
labs.note: Guided modules with labs. Some modules are paid.

Web Development.description: Build websites and web apps: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and backends.

courses.title: The Odin Project
courses.why: Project-based path from zero to full-stack. Needs self-discipline.

courses.title: freeCodeCamp Learn
courses.why: Code in the browser with instant feedback and projects.

courses.title: Learn web development
courses.why: Clear and accurate guides from the makers of the web docs.

courses.title: CS50's Web Programming with Python and JavaScript
courses.why: Django, JavaScript, APIs and deployment with graded projects.

notes.title: MDN Web Docs
notes.note: Reference for HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

notes.title: web.dev Learn
notes.note: Short courses on CSS, accessibility and performance.

labs.title: Frontend Mentor
labs.note: Real design challenges to build and compare.

labs.title: JavaScript30
labs.note: 30 small JavaScript projects (video course is free).

Machine Learning.description: Teach computers to learn from data. Needs basic Python and some math.

courses.title: Machine Learning Specialization
courses.why: The standard first ML course. Intuition first, then code labs.

courses.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
courses.why: Short, practical, with exercises. Good as a quick start.

courses.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
courses.why: Build real models first, learn theory after. Needs Python.

courses.title: CS229: Machine Learning
courses.why: Math-heavy university course with full lecture notes.

labs.title: Kaggle Learn
labs.note: Short free courses with notebooks you run online.

Data Structures & Algorithms.description: How to organize data and solve problems fast. Core of coding interviews.

courses.title: Algorithms (Khan Academy)
courses.why: Gentle visual start: searching, sorting, recursion.

courses.title: Algorithms, Part I
courses.why: Strong fundamentals. Examples use Java, ideas apply to any language.

courses.title: NeetCode Roadmap
courses.why: Topic-by-topic path with practice problems. Needs one language already.

courses.title: 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms (Spring 2020)
courses.why: University level with proofs, problem sets and lecture notes.

notes.title: CP-Algorithms
notes.note: Clear written explanations of many algorithms.

notes.title: VisuAlgo
notes.note: Animations of data structures and algorithms.

labs.title: LeetCode Problemset
labs.note: Filter by topic and difficulty. Start with Easy.

labs.title: NeetCode Practice
labs.note: Curated problem list with video solutions.
